page: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage capabilities include 2835 GB of local disk space, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance across several domains. The Intel processor's instruction set, which includes Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), supports strong cryptographic and integer operations, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU score of 68,963.55 and an encryption test score of 52,573.11. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches top-tier performance at 36.3 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression registers at 275.64 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is also strong, with read-only cached small block transfers reaching 3,733.43 GB/sec and uncached large block writes at 106.22 GB/sec.

In database and application workloads, the server achieves 84.18 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and scores 23,458.22 in Passmark database operations. Static web serving throughput is measured at 72.52 GB/sec. For machine learning tasks without a dedicated GPU, the CPU's AMX features enable strong LLM inference speeds, processing 2,691.32 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model and 28.93 tokens per second for text generation on a medium 7B model.

The D48ds_v7 offers a balanced resource density, combining high-frequency Intel Xeon processing with substantial local storage. This configuration provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high CPU throughput and local scratch space without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. Appropriate workloads include relational databases, Redis caching layers, static web serving, intermediate ETL pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
